caveats: POSTC General Notice 25-05 establishes statewide waiver history and eligibility, not the final Danbury enactment text.
The official Danbury Agenda Center still does not publish September 1 minutes at collection time, so the exact primary roll call and any final textual amendments remain unresolved.
No individual's citizenship, immigration status, or eligibility is inferred from these policy records.

conclusions: Issue #2514 can now distinguish statewide POSTC eligibility from Danbury's local ordinance: POSTC permits probationary-candidate eligibility for U.S. citizens, permanent legal residents, and DACA recipients through the cited waivers, while Danbury's local code amendment removes its stricter local citizenship barrier.

The policy change expands who may be considered; these records do not establish that any specific applicant or officer belongs to any immigration-status category, nor do they waive unrelated background, training, certification, or appointment requirements.
counterarguments: Published regulations can still display the older citizenship text even though POSTC exercised waiver authority; General Notice 25-05 explicitly documents that waiver mechanism and should not be collapsed into a claim that the regulation text itself was repealed.

Secondary reporting describes an 18-2 September 1 vote, but until the City's final minutes/adopted instrument are published that roll call and final text should remain source-qualified rather than promoted to primary-record fact.
findings: POSTC General Notice 25-05 is the authoritative state record tying lawful-permanent-resident eligibility to POSTC's November 19, 2020 partial waiver and DACA-recipient eligibility to its March 13, 2025 further waiver.
The notice identifies the waiver authority as CGS § 7-294d(a)(20) and the underlying citizenship regulation as RCSA § 7-294e-16(c), and says POSTC-51 was updated to reflect the eligibility change.
Danbury's previously captured proposal-stage section 22-27(a) language therefore has a concrete state-policy alignment surface rather than merely a media-described rationale.

As of September 15, 2026 the official Danbury City Council Agenda Center exposes the September 1 agenda but no minutes or media link, so the final adopted wording, named 18-2 roll call, effective date, and formal enactment identifier remain primary-record gaps.
unresolved: September 1, 2026 final City Council minutes and named roll call, including the two NO votes.

summary: Authoritative POSTC notice resolves the statewide eligibility bridge behind Danbury's 2026 amendment: LPR eligibility dates to the November 2020 waiver and DACA eligibility to the March 13, 2025 further waiver; Danbury's final primary September record remains unpublished in the official Agenda Center at collection time.
